A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAC Flow. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including the new Appendix F in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original MuJoCo, OGBench, and Robomimic experiments, including learning curves and architecture and sampling-step ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds adapter fine-tuning experiments in Figures 16–17.

M1.justification: Appendix F adds an adapter-based fine-tuning algorithm. Flow-G gates a frozen pretrained velocity network instead of using its original gated residual velocity; Flow-T incorporates the pretrained network into its decoder formulation. Algorithm 3 introduces behavioral-cloning actor warm-up before regularized SAC updates. The original methods remain.

E1.justification: Reported task and dataset coverage remains MuJoCo locomotion, OGBench cube manipulation, and Robomimic Lift, Can, and Square. Fine-tuning uses existing tasks. Deleting the scene-sparse hyperparameter row from Table 4 does not establish removal of an evaluated task; neither version reports corresponding results.

E2.justification: New Figures 16–17 use the original SAC Flow-G and SAC Flow-T as reference methods against their adapter fine-tuning variants. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark experiments is unchanged, including DIME, FlowRL, QSM, SAC, PPO, FQL, QC-FQL, and ReinFlow where applicable.

E3.justification: The added fine-tuning experiments introduce a distinct training protocol: 1M flow-matching pretraining steps, a freshly initialized critic, 0.1M warm-up steps with a behavioral-cloning actor objective, and 1M subsequent online interaction steps. This supplements rather than revises the original experimental protocols.

E4.justification: The velocity-network, gradient-norm, and sampling-step ablations in Figures 6–7 and 12–13 are retained. Figure 7 changes visual styling. The added adapter benchmark results do not provide a separate controlled test of the proposed critic-initialization explanation.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results use five random seeds and 95% confidence intervals. No changed repetition count, uncertainty-estimation procedure, or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: Figure 4 revises MuJoCo curves and rankings. In Humanoid, the gray curve labeled PPO changes from below 500 to about 11,000 return at 1M steps, exceeding SAC Flow in v3. Its intended attribution is unclear because the revised prose instead describes competitive DIME results. Figures 16–17 also add fine-tuning results for ten OGBench and three Robomimic tasks under the new protocol.

T1.justification: Appendix F adds mathematical definitions of the adapter velocities and warm-up objective, plus an initialization argument for preserving pretrained behavior. The original flow/RNN correspondence and Appendix A likelihood and SAC derivations are unchanged; no additional stability proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces broad claims of superior returns and convergence with benchmark-specific claims of gains up to 130% on MuJoCo and 60% on OGBench. The central contributions concerning sequential parameterization, gradient stability, and direct SAC training remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 now acknowledges the Humanoid exception and comparable performance on HalfCheetah and Ant. Appendix F newly suggests that a randomly initialized critic may be easier to optimize online than an offline-pretrained critic. The existing explanation involving strong Robomimic regularization is retained.

D1.justification: Appendix F supplies adapter-specific freezing, initialization, warm-up, and update instructions, including zero-initialized Transformer blocks. Table 4 removes the scene-sparse regularization row. Existing implementation tables and the code access URL otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and extended related-work discussion are unchanged, including positioning against diffusion policies, FlowRL, and distillation-based offline-to-online methods.

P1.justification: Localized edits revise the contribution statement and results discussion, shorten future-work prose, update affiliations, and introduce Appendix F with a main-text pointer. The overall organization and most explanations are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 16–17 and Algorithm 3, moves Figure 15 to the following page, changes Figure 7 line styles, recolors QC-FQL curves, and adjusts Figure 4 axes and caption. Table 4 loses one row; the overall visual format remains.

improvement.justification: Appendix F makes pretrained-policy adaptation more concrete through an algorithm and experiments, while the Humanoid qualification corrects an overly broad performance claim. However, revised Figure 4 conflicts with its accompanying DIME discussion: the competitive gray curve remains labeled PPO. This unresolved attribution affects central baseline comparisons. The practical additions and weakened clarity of comparative evidence prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
